rules.statement: Values declared in operational-register fields of .intent/ artifacts MUST match the Operational-register grammar `^[a-z][a-z0-9_]*$`. Operational-register fields include: `authority`, `phase`, `enforcement`, `status`, `class`, and `ordering.mode`. The operational-register enum vocabularies declared in `.intent/META/enums.json` MUST likewise use this grammar, including `audit_severity` (ADR-059 D2 moved severity from the Diagnostic to the Operational register; ADR-158 D1 conforms this paper's register-assignment table to that decision). A value such as `authority: Policy` (Title Case) or `phase: AUDIT` (UPPER_CASE) imports the wrong register into an Operational-register field and is governance failure. (2026-08-31, ADR-158 D2/D3: `strength` and bare `ordering` were dropped from the field list -- `strength` names the enum's own vocabulary key in `enums.json`, not an authored field name; the authored field is `enforcement`. Bare `ordering` is always a nested config block in every live artifact, never a scalar; the real governed leaf is the nested `ordering.mode`, per `enums.json`'s `workflow_ordering_mode` enum. See #854.)
rules.rationale: Operational-register values are routing keys joined and dispatched on across Python, YAML, JSON, and SQL. A casing mismatch silently breaks loaders that compare case-sensitively, or propagates inconsistent forms through tolerant loaders. Article I S5 of the Constitution declares the three registers; this rule enforces that operational fields stay in the Operational register. `severity` was added to this rule's governed surface 2026-08-31 (ADR-158 D1) after `governance.vocabulary_registers.diagnostic_fields_must_be_uppercase` was retired (see that rule's own entry) -- the Diagnostic register has no remaining `.intent/`-authored surface, and severity's real casing requirement (ADR-059 D2, lowercase) belongs here. See `.specs/papers/CORE-Vocabulary-Registers.md` for the doctrinal source and the full register-assignment table.

rules.statement: RETIRED (2026-08-31, ADR-158, #854). No live .intent/-authored diagnostic-register surface exists to enforce against: severity was reclassified to the Operational register (ADR-059 D2; see governance.vocabulary_registers.operational_fields_must_be_lowercase, which now governs it), and verdict states (PASS/FAIL/DEGRADED) -- the Diagnostic register's only remaining assigned concept-family per CORE-Vocabulary-Registers.md S5 -- are computed at runtime and never authored as static .intent/ content (confirmed by a corpus-wide search across every .intent/**/*.yaml and *.json file, ADR-158 Context). Append-only closure marker: rule retained as historical record; enforcement downgraded to advisory; mapping entry removed so no findings are dispatched. Reinstatement trigger: if a diagnostic-register field is ever authored into .intent/ as static content, or verdict states become static content, this rule (or a successor) should be revived against that real surface -- not before.
rules.rationale: Originally targeted severity fields and verdict-state fields under the (then-doctrinally-consistent) claim that the Diagnostic register requires UPPER_CASE. ADR-059 D2 (accepted 2026-05-19) retired that casing for severity specifically, and the paper (CORE-Vocabulary-Registers.md) was never updated to match -- this rule's own statement carried a stale historical note acknowledging the mismatch for over a year without anyone resolving it, discovered during #854's G2 fixture-coverage depth-verification. Verdict states were never touched by ADR-059 D2 and remain Diagnostic-register content in principle, but a corpus-wide search found zero live .intent/-authored instances -- they are computed at runtime, never authored statically. With severity reclassified (ADR-158 D1) and verdict states never live, this rule has no real surface left to check; retiring it is more honest than declaring an enforcement_location that would forever find nothing.
